effect: Refined lunar metal brought back to Earth is valued at an Earth commodity price, USD 10 000 a tonne (about titanium sponge; iron, aluminium and silicon are cheaper), instead of USD 80 million a tonne, in the value of a return cargo (qCa, the value the AI weighs against a return flight's cost; it flew metal home whenever that value was twice the flight cost). On Earth the metal saves no launch mass, so it is worth what the same metal costs from a terrestrial producer. Using the metal keeps the game's value (design decision, 2026-11-18: 'separate the two'): a module order still credits 0.08 bn per tonne of the stock it uses, up to 20 % of its cost (w3t and the module quote are unchanged), so an order uses the same tonnage as before and the stock is not swept for a token credit. Helium-3 and Mars deposits keep their own prices; converting metal into research credits is unchanged. Real-world basis: titanium sponge trades at roughly USD 10 000 a tonne, steel and aluminium far less (USGS Mineral Commodity Summaries); in-space resources are valued for the launch mass they replace, which applies only off Earth. No day-0 effect (no metal stock at day 0). No new state. Minified names are those of build 26734764.
